scope.summary: This standard specifies standard methods, billing frameworks, and technical criteria for measuring topographical survey work (including alignments of canals, drains, highways, and cross-section surveys) performed in river valley projects to ensure contractual transparency and uniform cost analysis.

version_status_and_amendments.edition_year_of_copy: First Revision, 2026 (developed to integrate modern total station, GIS-based, and computerized surveying measurement systems into standard river valley contract billing frameworks)
version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: No active amendments have been issued on this newly established 2026 standard (NIL on this copy).

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Procedural and Measurement Code of Practice (Water Resources Department)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Measurement Code. Since IS 9401 (Part 12) is a standard method of measurement and quantity auditing rather than a physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, its use is strictly mandated by the Central Water Commission (CWC), state water resources departments, public sector utilities (such as NHPC, BBMB, THDC, WAPCOS, SJVN), and civil auditing boards across India. It is universally incorporated into commercial tender specifications, construction contracts, and billing schedules of public works to determine contractors' payments, measure physical excavation quantities, and prevent contractual disputes. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Mandates that topographical measurements, specifically cross-section surveys, must be carried out and recorded on a standardized linear basis (e.g., per running metre or kilometre).

Specifies that the topographical and cross-sectional surveys must cover and map specific key features, including alignments of canals, natural drainages, highways, and other similar linear elements of the river valley project.
Cross-sectional measurements must comprehensively include all individual work items, pegging, benchmarking, leveling, and clearance activities as specified under Clause 3.4 of the standard.
Integrates topographical surveying techniques and scales with the guidelines of IS 5497 to ensure appropriate contour resolutions and surveying accuracies are maintained across the project command.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 9401 (Part 12) : 2026 is the national Indian Standard establishing standard methods of measurement for topographical surveys in river valley projects, specifically for dams and appurtenant structures. Prepared by the WRD 23 committee, this standard provides a uniform technical framework to measure and bill surveying activities (such as cross-section and alignment surveys for canals, drains, and highways) on a linear basis. It serves as a vital contractual and quantity auditing code across major hydropower and irrigation projects in India, ensuring that all cost analysis and quantity auditing practices remain objective, transparent, and consistent with modern surveying technology.
